rows.rowHtml: 1913Markov chainsStatistical models of state-to-state transitions. The mathematical seed of language modeling, HMMs and reinforcement learning's state formalism.ROOTS · MATH, NEURO & CYBERNETICSDevelopment; Foundational

1879-1928Formal logic program (Frege→Hilbert)The project of reducing reasoning to symbol manipulation. Made 'thinking machines' conceivable before computers existed.ROOTS · MATH, NEURO & CYBERNETICSDevelopment; Foundational

1931Gödel incompletenessGödel showed that any consistent, effectively axiomatized formal system expressive enough for arithmetic contains true statements it cannot prove. This bounds mechanized reasoning without precluding useful automation.ROOTS · MATH, NEURO & CYBERNETICSDevelopment; Foundational

1936Turing machineTuring formalized computation with an abstract universal machine. Most digital AI software fits this computational model, while analog and quantum systems extend the hardware story.ROOTS · MATH, NEURO & CYBERNETICSDevelopment; Foundational
1937Boolean circuits (Shannon's thesis)Switching circuits implement logic. The bridge from abstract symbols to physical hardware.ROOTS · MATH, NEURO & CYBERNETICSDevelopment; Foundational

1943McCulloch–Pitts neuronMcCulloch and Pitts modeled idealized neurons as logical threshold units, creating an early bridge from neurobiology to artificial neural computation.ROOTS · MATH, NEURO & CYBERNETICSDevelopment; Foundational

1944Game theory (von Neumann–Morgenstern)Strategic rationality formalized. Underpins multi-agent AI, GANs, poker solvers and mechanism design.ROOTS · MATH, NEURO & CYBERNETICSDevelopment; Foundational

1945Stored-program computerStored-program architecture became computing's dominant general-purpose substrate. Specialized accelerators retain it at system level, while neuromorphic, analog and quantum approaches explore alternatives to the von Neumann bottleneck.ROOTS · MATH, NEURO & CYBERNETICSDevelopment; Foundational

1948Cybernetics (Wiener)Feedback, control and communication in animal and machine. Seeded AI, control theory, robotics and the first misalignment worries.ROOTS · MATH, NEURO & CYBERNETICSDevelopment; Foundational
1948Information theoryInformation quantified; prediction and compression unified. The deep reason language modeling works at all.ROOTS · MATH, NEURO & CYBERNETICSDevelopment; Foundational

1949Hebbian learningHebbian learning linked correlated neural activity to synaptic change and remains foundational in associative and biologically plausible learning; modern gradient updates are not generally Hebbian.ROOTS · MATH, NEURO & CYBERNETICSDevelopment; Foundational

1950Turing test'Computing Machinery and Intelligence' reframed 'can machines think?' as an imitation game. The field's north star and favorite argument.ROOTS · MATH, NEURO & CYBERNETICSDevelopment; Foundational
1952Hodgkin–Huxley neuron modelThe biophysics of the spike, measured and modeled. Ground truth for spiking networks and neuromorphic silicon.ROOTS · MATH, NEURO & CYBERNETICSDevelopment; Foundational

1956Dartmouth workshop — 'AI' namedMcCarthy, Minsky, Shannon, Rochester bet a summer could crack intelligence. Wrong on timing, right on ambition — the field's founding myth.ROOTS · MATH, NEURO & CYBERNETICSDevelopment; Foundational
1956Cognitive revolutionMiller, Chomsky, Newell & Simon recast mind as information processing. Psychology and AI were born entangled.ROOTS · MATH, NEURO & CYBERNETICSDevelopment; Foundational

1959Hubel & Wiesel visual cortexOrientation-selective cells stacked in layers — the biological blueprint later copied by the neocognitron and CNNs.ROOTS · MATH, NEURO & CYBERNETICSDevelopment; Foundational

1964Solomonoff inductionUniversal prediction by weighting all programs by simplicity. The idealized learner behind AIXI and compression-based views of intelligence.ROOTS · MATH, NEURO & CYBERNETICSDevelopment; Foundational

1965Kolmogorov complexity & MDLLearning as compression, formalized. Quietly resurfaces in every era — most recently in 'compression is intelligence' scaling arguments.ROOTS · MATH, NEURO & CYBERNETICSDevelopment; Foundational

1971NP-completeness (Cook–Karp)Which problems are intractable. Explains why naive search-based AI hit walls — and why heuristics and learning are necessary.ROOTS · MATH, NEURO & CYBERNETICSDevelopment; Foundational

1980Chinese Room & symbol groundingSearle: syntax isn't semantics. The grounding critique haunted symbolic AI; multimodal, embodied learning is the modern rebuttal-in-progress.ROOTS · MATH, NEURO & CYBERNETICSDevelopment; Foundational

1988Symbolic vs connectionist warFodor & Pylyshyn: can networks compose meaning? The systematicity debate — reopened, not settled, by LLM reasoning.ROOTS · MATH, NEURO & CYBERNETICSDevelopment; Foundational

2005Free-energy principleFriston: brains minimize prediction error. Grand, contested, hard to operationalize — the neuroscience shadow of world-model AI.ROOTS · MATH, NEURO & CYBERNETICSDevelopment; Active

2026Active inference at scaleResearch direction: test whether active-inference objectives can support competitive, large-scale agents. Existing work has not yet established parity with frontier-scale model-based agents.ROOTS · MATH, NEURO & CYBERNETICSOpen direction; Open direction
1956Logic TheoristNewell & Simon's first AI program — proved theorems from Principia by heuristic search over symbols. AI's opening move.SYMBOLIC AI & KNOWLEDGEDevelopment; Foundational
1958LISPMcCarthy's symbolic language: code as data, recursion, garbage collection. AI's native tongue for 30 years.SYMBOLIC AI & KNOWLEDGEDevelopment; Foundational

1959General Problem SolverMeans–ends analysis as a theory of thought. 'General' proved elusive beyond puzzles — but it seeded planning and cognitive architectures.SYMBOLIC AI & KNOWLEDGEDevelopment; Foundational
1959Advice Taker & the logicist creedMcCarthy's program: represent knowledge as logical sentences, act by deduction. The purist wing of symbolic AI.SYMBOLIC AI & KNOWLEDGEDevelopment; Foundational

1965Resolution theorem provingRobinson's single complete inference rule made automated deduction real — and revealed combinatorial explosion as the enemy.SYMBOLIC AI & KNOWLEDGEDevelopment; Foundational

1965DENDRAL — first expert systemMass-spectrometry chemistry via encoded expertise. Proved domain knowledge beats general search — the knowledge turn begins.SYMBOLIC AI & KNOWLEDGEDevelopment; Foundational
1966Semantic networksQuillian's concepts-as-graphs. Ancestor of frames, ontologies, knowledge graphs — and, arguably, of embeddings-as-relations.SYMBOLIC AI & KNOWLEDGEDevelopment; Foundational

1970SHRDLU & blocks worldWinograd's dazzling language-plus-planning demo in a toy world. Famously refused to scale — the archetype of the demo-to-world gap.SYMBOLIC AI & KNOWLEDGEDevelopment; Ended / superseded (legacy)

1972Prolog & logic programmingComputation as deduction. Once a national strategy (Japan bet on it); now a respected niche in verification, Datalog and answer-set programming.SYMBOLIC AI & KNOWLEDGEDevelopment; Dormant

1973-1980Lighthill Report → first AI winterUK review damning AI's unmet promises; with DARPA cuts it froze funding for a decade. The field's first reckoning with its own hype.SYMBOLIC AI & KNOWLEDGEDevelopment; Ended / superseded (legacy)

1974MYCINRule-based infection diagnosis that rivaled experts — and was never deployed (liability, integration, trust). The expert-system template and its fate in one system.SYMBOLIC AI & KNOWLEDGEDevelopment; Ended / superseded (legacy)

1974Frames (Minsky)Structured slots and defaults for commonsense knowledge. Ancestor of objects, schemas, ontologies — and of every 'context' hack since.SYMBOLIC AI & KNOWLEDGEDevelopment; Foundational
1976AM & EURISKOLenat's discovery programs invented concepts, won wargame tournaments — then 'ran out of steam.' Their post-mortem led him to Cyc.SYMBOLIC AI & KNOWLEDGEDevelopment; Dormant

1980Blackboard architecturesHEARSAY-II's shared-workspace coordination of specialist modules. Faded — yet echoes in every multi-agent orchestration framework today.SYMBOLIC AI & KNOWLEDGEDevelopment; Dormant

1980XCON at DECConfigured VAX orders with 10,000+ rules, saved ~$40M/yr — then drowned in rule-maintenance. The boom's flagship and its cautionary tale.SYMBOLIC AI & KNOWLEDGEDevelopment; Ended / superseded (legacy)

1980Non-monotonic logic & frame problemFormalizing defeasible commonsense reasoning. Non-monotonic logics provide rigorous tools, while the broader frame problem remains open and many practical systems use learned or domain-specific workarounds.SYMBOLIC AI & KNOWLEDGEDevelopment; Dormant

1981Expert-systems industryShells, consultancies, and knowledge engineers turned expert systems into an industry. Lisp-machine workstations helped enable the boom; brittle rules and costly upkeep helped collapse it by 1990.SYMBOLIC AI & KNOWLEDGEDevelopment; Ended / superseded (legacy)

1980Lisp machinesA whole hardware industry (Symbolics, LMI) for symbolic AI — wiped out by commodity workstations by 1987. Hardware bet on a software fad.SYMBOLIC AI & KNOWLEDGEDevelopment; Ended / superseded (legacy)

1982Fifth Generation ProjectJapan's $850M national bet on massively parallel logic programming. Delivered little; its shadow scared funders worldwide for a decade.SYMBOLIC AI & KNOWLEDGEDevelopment; Ended / superseded (legacy)

1983SOAR & ACT-R architecturesUnified theories of cognition with dedicated labs for decades — marginal to modern AI, but a likely quarry for LLM-agent memory design.SYMBOLIC AI & KNOWLEDGEDevelopment; Dormant

1983Case-based reasoningSolve new problems by adapting stored cases. A thriving 90s subfield that faded to niche — conceptually reborn as retrieval-augmented everything.SYMBOLIC AI & KNOWLEDGEDevelopment; Dormant

1984Cyc — commonsense by handLenat's 40-year, million-axiom quest to hand-encode common sense. The grandest knowledge-engineering grind; still no general reasoner emerged.SYMBOLIC AI & KNOWLEDGEDevelopment; Dormant

1988Second AI winterExpert-system market collapse plus Lisp-machine crash. 'AI' became a dirty word; survivors rebranded as 'machine learning.'SYMBOLIC AI & KNOWLEDGEDevelopment; Ended / superseded (legacy)

1989Interactive theorem proversCoq→Isabelle→Lean: humans and machines formalizing mathematics. A quiet community for 30 years — now the verification substrate for AI mathematicians.SYMBOLIC AI & KNOWLEDGEDevelopment; Revived

1991Inductive logic programmingLearning logic rules from examples. Elegant, interpretable, data-inefficient — sidelined by statistical ML; small revival alongside program synthesis.SYMBOLIC AI & KNOWLEDGEDevelopment; Dormant

1991Description logics & ontologiesDecidable fragments of logic for taxonomies; became OWL. Industrial ontology work persists; the research frontier moved on.SYMBOLIC AI & KNOWLEDGEDevelopment; Dormant
1965Fuzzy logicZadeh's graded truth. Ran 80s–90s consumer devices (cameras, rice cookers, trains), then drifted out of core AI research entirely.SYMBOLIC AI & KNOWLEDGEDevelopment; Dormant

2001Semantic Web (RDF/OWL)RDF and OWL standardized a machine-readable web of linked facts. The universal Semantic Web vision receded, but the standards persist in knowledge graphs and linked-data systems.SYMBOLIC AI & KNOWLEDGEDevelopment; Dormant
2012Knowledge graphs at scaleGoogle KG, Wikidata: semantic networks reborn industrially. Now the structured complement — and grounding source — for LLMs.SYMBOLIC AI & KNOWLEDGEDevelopment; Revived

2019Neuro-symbolic AIMarrying networks and symbols: program synthesis, tool use, logic-guided decoding. Perennial hope, real progress, no unified paradigm yet.SYMBOLIC AI & KNOWLEDGEDevelopment; Active

2026Symbolic rigor at LLM scaleResearch direction: combine broad language-model capabilities with end-to-end formal verification. Current systems demonstrate verified reasoning in bounded mathematics and code settings; broad coverage remains unresolved.SYMBOLIC AI & KNOWLEDGEOpen direction; Open direction
1950Shannon's chess blueprint'Programming a Computer for Playing Chess': minimax plus evaluation functions. The founding document of game AI.SEARCH, PLANNING & GAMESDevelopment; Foundational
1958Alpha–beta & heuristic searchPruning cut game trees exponentially; heuristic evaluation made search practical. The workhorse of classical AI.SEARCH, PLANNING & GAMESDevelopment; Foundational
1968A* searchOptimal pathfinding with admissible heuristics, built for Shakey. In every router, game engine and planner since.SEARCH, PLANNING & GAMESDevelopment; Foundational
1971STRIPS planningActions as precondition/effect schemas. The planning formalism — and the stage on which the frame problem performed.SEARCH, PLANNING & GAMESDevelopment; Foundational

1977Constraint satisfactionWaltz line-labeling to Mackworth's arc consistency: propagate constraints instead of searching blindly. Scheduling and layout still run on it.SEARCH, PLANNING & GAMESDevelopment; Foundational

1994Checkers conquered (Chinook)First program to win a world title from humans; checkers fully solved by 2007. Proof of how far brute search + endgame tables go.SEARCH, PLANNING & GAMESDevelopment; Foundational

1997Deep Blue beats Kasparov200M positions/sec plus hand-tuned evaluation topples chess. Taught two lessons: search scales, and chess wasn't intelligence after all.SEARCH, PLANNING & GAMESDevelopment; Foundational

1998Classical planning & PDDLMature solvers, annual competitions, logistics benchmarks — then a plateau outside them. Now probed again as scaffolding for LLM agents.SEARCH, PLANNING & GAMESDevelopment; Dormant
2001Modern SAT/SMT solversCDCL made logical search industrial: chip verification, software analysis. Symbolic AI's quietest, most deployed victory.SEARCH, PLANNING & GAMESDevelopment; Active

2006Monte Carlo Tree SearchRandom rollouts + bandit selection cracked Go's branching factor. The bridge from classical search to AlphaGo — and to test-time reasoning.SEARCH, PLANNING & GAMESDevelopment; Foundational

2017Imperfect-info games solvedLibratus and Pluribus beat top pros via counterfactual regret minimization. Game theory made computational — then the labs moved on.SEARCH, PLANNING & GAMESDevelopment; Foundational

2023LLM-guided searchTree-of-Thoughts, planner hybrids, verifier-guided decoding: classical search reborn with learned heuristics. The search lane merges into the LLM lane.SEARCH, PLANNING & GAMESDevelopment; Hot frontier

1952Multi-armed banditsRobbins formalized explore-vs-exploit. From clinical trials to UCB — the mathematical kernel inside MCTS and every recommender.REINFORCEMENT LEARNING & AGENTSDevelopment; Foundational

1957MDPs & Bellman equationsA mathematical framework for sequential decisions under uncertainty, with dynamic programming and Bellman equations underpinning many planning and value-based reinforcement-learning methods.REINFORCEMENT LEARNING & AGENTSDevelopment; Foundational

1959Samuel's checkers learnerSelf-play plus a learned evaluation on 1950s hardware — machine learning's public debut and TD learning's ancestor.REINFORCEMENT LEARNING & AGENTSDevelopment; Foundational

1988Temporal-difference learningSutton: learn predictions from later predictions. RL's core algorithmic idea — later found running in dopamine neurons.REINFORCEMENT LEARNING & AGENTSDevelopment; Foundational
1989Q-learningWatkins' off-policy value learning with a convergence proof. Tabular RL matured — then waited 24 years for deep nets.REINFORCEMENT LEARNING & AGENTSDevelopment; Foundational
1992TD-GammonNeural net + TD self-play reached top-human backgammon. The AlphaGo recipe, 24 years early — then largely ignored for a decade.REINFORCEMENT LEARNING & AGENTSDevelopment; Foundational

1992-2000Policy gradients (REINFORCE → actor–critic)REINFORCE optimized policies directly from sampled returns; actor–critic methods paired that policy with a learned value function. This is the missing bridge to PPO and RLHF.REINFORCEMENT LEARNING & AGENTSDevelopment; Foundational

1997Dopamine = TD errorSchultz's recordings matched TD prediction error. Neuroscience validated RL's core signal — a rare two-way street between AI and brain.REINFORCEMENT LEARNING & AGENTSDevelopment; Foundational
1998RL synthesis (Sutton & Barto)REINFORCE, actor-critic, the textbook. Reinforcement learning becomes a coherent field with a shared language.REINFORCEMENT LEARNING & AGENTSDevelopment; Foundational

1999Hierarchical RL (options)Temporal abstraction: learn skills, compose them. Perennially promising, perpetually stuck — LLM planners now route around it from above.REINFORCEMENT LEARNING & AGENTSDevelopment; Dormant

2013DQN — Atari from pixelsDeep nets + Q-learning + experience replay: one algorithm, 49 games, superhuman on many. Deep RL ignites (and DeepMind gets acquired).REINFORCEMENT LEARNING & AGENTSDevelopment; Foundational

2016AlphaGo beats Lee SedolPolicy/value networks + MCTS + self-play. Move 37 became the era's cultural shockwave — a decade ahead of expert predictions.REINFORCEMENT LEARNING & AGENTSDevelopment; Foundational

2017AlphaZero / MuZeroTabula-rasa self-play mastering Go, chess, shogi; MuZero learns the rules too. Search and learning unified — the lane's high-water mark.REINFORCEMENT LEARNING & AGENTSDevelopment; Foundational

2015-2017Policy-gradient workhorses (PPO)A3C introduced asynchronous actor-critic training, and PPO became a common early optimization method for RLHF as well as a durable control baseline; later preference-training systems also use several alternatives.REINFORCEMENT LEARNING & AGENTSDevelopment; Foundational

2017Curiosity & intrinsic motivationRewards from novelty and prediction error. Hot 2017–19, then faded — exploration at scale remains genuinely unsolved.REINFORCEMENT LEARNING & AGENTSDevelopment; Dormant
2017Multi-agent RLEmergent cooperation, competition and tool use (hide-and-seek). Re-energized by LLM agent societies and mechanism-design questions.REINFORCEMENT LEARNING & AGENTSDevelopment; Active

2018World Models (Ha & Schmidhuber)VAE+RNN agent trained inside its own learned dream. The seed of today's world-model wave — imagination as a training ground.REINFORCEMENT LEARNING & AGENTSDevelopment; Foundational

2019Model-based RL (Dreamer)Learn the world, plan in imagination. The sample-efficiency path that matured into world-model agents for robots and games.REINFORCEMENT LEARNING & AGENTSDevelopment; Active

2019OpenAI Five & AlphaStarSuperhuman Dota 2 and StarCraft II via massive self-play. Peak-then-pivot: point proven, labs promptly abandoned esports for language.REINFORCEMENT LEARNING & AGENTSDevelopment; Foundational

2019Open-endedness (POET)Systems that endlessly generate their own challenges. Niche but philosophically central — the question behind 'never-ending' agents.REINFORCEMENT LEARNING & AGENTSDevelopment; Active

2020Offline RL & sequence policiesLearn policies from logged trajectories without online exploration. Distribution shift remains hard, while Decision Transformer reframed policy learning as sequence modeling and the field feeds robotics and preference pipelines.REINFORCEMENT LEARNING & AGENTSDevelopment; Active

2022Generalist agents (Gato)One transformer, 600 tasks, none mastered. Scaling alone didn't cure breadth-without-depth; quietly shelved as LLM agents took the crown.REINFORCEMENT LEARNING & AGENTSDevelopment; Dormant

2023LLM agents & tool useReAct→computer use→autonomous coding: language models that act. 2025–26's dominant paradigm — and its reliability problem.REINFORCEMENT LEARNING & AGENTSDevelopment; Hot frontier

2024RL on verifiable rewardsTrain reasoning against checkable answers (math, code, proofs). The engine of o1/R1-class models — RL's biggest win since AlphaGo.REINFORCEMENT LEARNING & AGENTSDevelopment; Hot frontier

2026Robust, general open-ended self-improvementSelf-generated tasks and self-editing agents now show bounded improvement under human-designed verifiers. Still missing: safe, broadly general, sustained improvement without benchmark gaming, collapse, or a fixed external objective.REINFORCEMENT LEARNING & AGENTSOpen direction; Open direction

1958Perceptron (Rosenblatt)Hardware neuron that learned from examples; the Navy promised it would 'walk, talk, see, write.' The hype and the machine that started it all.NEURAL ARCHITECTURESDevelopment; Foundational
1960ADALINE & delta ruleWidrow–Hoff gradient learning in analog hardware. LMS still runs in every modem — neural nets' first quiet deployment.NEURAL ARCHITECTURESDevelopment; Foundational

1969'Perceptrons' kills the fieldMinsky & Papert proved single-layer limits (XOR); funding evaporated for 15 years. The canonical premature burial — multilayer nets weren't disproven, just undone.NEURAL ARCHITECTURESDevelopment; Ended / superseded (legacy)
1980NeocognitronFukushima stacked Hubel–Wiesel receptive fields into a deep hierarchy. CNNs before backprop — an idea waiting 30 years for compute.NEURAL ARCHITECTURESDevelopment; Foundational

1982Hopfield networksEnergy-based associative memory that re-legitimized neural research. Faded for decades — then 'modern Hopfield' math turned out to equal attention. 2024 Nobel.NEURAL ARCHITECTURESDevelopment; Revived
1985Boltzmann machinesStochastic energy models with hidden units. Training pain sidelined them, but their DNA lives in RBMs, energy-based models and diffusion.NEURAL ARCHITECTURESDevelopment; Dormant

1986Restricted Boltzmann machinesSmolensky's bipartite Harmonium made Boltzmann machines easier to train; contrastive divergence revived it in the mid-2000s. Stacking RBMs supplied the pretraining recipe for deep belief networks.NEURAL ARCHITECTURESDevelopment; Foundational

1986BackpropagationRumelhart–Hinton–Williams popularized credit assignment through layers (roots: Linnainmaa '70, Werbos '74). THE algorithm of the modern era.NEURAL ARCHITECTURESDevelopment; Foundational
1986PDP & connectionism revivalThe two-volume manifesto that brought neural nets back into cognitive science and AI. Winter number one, officially over.NEURAL ARCHITECTURESDevelopment; Foundational
1989Universal approximationMLPs can represent any function — existence, not learnability. Comfort, and false comfort, for a generation of theorists.NEURAL ARCHITECTURESDevelopment; Foundational
1989LeNet CNNsLeCun fused neocognitron structure with backprop; read ~10% of US checks by the late 90s. Then waited 15 years for its GPU moment.NEURAL ARCHITECTURESDevelopment; Foundational
1990Recurrent networksElman nets and backprop-through-time: sequence processing with memory. NLP's neural substrate until 2017.NEURAL ARCHITECTURESDevelopment; Foundational

1991Vanishing-gradient diagnosisHochreiter's analysis of why depth wouldn't train. The diagnosis behind LSTM, pretraining detours, and eventually residual connections.NEURAL ARCHITECTURESDevelopment; Foundational
1997LSTMGated memory defeats vanishing gradients. Carried speech and translation until 2017 — then dethroned by the transformer.NEURAL ARCHITECTURESDevelopment; Foundational

2006Deep belief nets & pretrainingLayer-wise stacks of restricted Boltzmann machines re-ignited deep learning, then were superseded once ReLU networks and GPUs trained effectively end to end. A historically important transitional method.NEURAL ARCHITECTURESDevelopment; Ended / superseded (legacy)
2006AutoencodersCompression as self-supervision. Ancestor of VAEs, masked pretraining, and the representation-learning worldview.NEURAL ARCHITECTURESDevelopment; Foundational
2014Attention mechanismBahdanau's soft alignment for translation: look where it matters. The seed the transformer grew from.NEURAL ARCHITECTURESDevelopment; Foundational

2014Neural Turing Machines / DNCDifferentiable external memory. Beautiful, barely trainable, abandoned — yet it foreshadowed tool use, RAG and memory-augmented agents.NEURAL ARCHITECTURESDevelopment; Ended / superseded (legacy)
2015ResNet — residual connectionsSkip connections let 100+ layers train. In literally everything since, transformers included. Depth's final unlock.NEURAL ARCHITECTURESDevelopment; Foundational

2016Hypernetworks & fast weightsNetworks generating other networks' weights. Never mainstream, but conceptually adjacent to LoRA, in-context learning and test-time adaptation.NEURAL ARCHITECTURESDevelopment; Dormant

2017Transformer'Attention Is All You Need': ditch recurrence, keep attention, parallelize everything. The architecture of the modern era — still unseated in 2026.NEURAL ARCHITECTURESDevelopment; Foundational
2017Graph neural networksMessage passing on graphs. The 2018–21 hype cooled; quietly indispensable in chemistry, chip design and weather.NEURAL ARCHITECTURESDevelopment; Active

2017Capsule networksPart–whole representations with learned routing offered an alternative to conventional CNNs. They did not become a mainstream replacement, but remain a specialist research line rather than a proven impossibility.NEURAL ARCHITECTURESDevelopment; Ended / superseded (legacy)

2018Neural ODEsNeural networks parameterize continuous-time dynamics solved by differential-equation methods. Adoption is specialized but active in time series, control, scientific machine learning, and continuous normalizing flows.NEURAL ARCHITECTURESDevelopment; Active

2017Mixture-of-ExpertsConditional compute: route each token through a sliver of a huge model. A 1991 idea that became the standard frontier architecture (Mixtral, DeepSeek-V3).NEURAL ARCHITECTURESDevelopment; Active

2020Linear-attention wavePerformer, RWKV, and related methods sought subquadratic alternatives to exact attention. Better kernels narrowed the case, but recurrent and linear-attention variants remain an active efficiency niche and influenced state-space models.NEURAL ARCHITECTURESDevelopment; Dormant

2021-2023State-space models (S4→Mamba)Linear-time sequence modeling rooted in control theory. S4 and Mamba revived state-space models as competitive sequence architectures; hybrid attention-SSM designs are active and relative performance remains task- and scale-dependent.NEURAL ARCHITECTURESDevelopment; Active

2025Test-time memory (Titans)Architectures whose weights update while running — nested learning against frozen-model amnesia. The architectural frontier of 2025–26.NEURAL ARCHITECTURESDevelopment; Hot frontier

2026Energy-based LMs at scaleResearch direction: compare energy-based, diffusion-language-model and JEPA-style non-autoregressive systems with strong autoregressive baselines at equal data, parameter, inference-compute and latency budgets. Capable 8B-14B non-autoregressive systems already exist; robust parity across broad language tasks, efficiency and controllability remains unresolved.NEURAL ARCHITECTURESOpen direction; Open direction

1951Stochastic gradient descentRobbins–Monro stochastic approximation. The humble optimizer that, with tweaks, trained everything from ADALINE to GPT.TRAINING, SCALE & EFFICIENCYDevelopment; Foundational

1989Catastrophic forgetting identifiedMcCloskey & Cohen: networks overwrite old skills when learning new ones. The 35-year-old bug that still defines the continual-learning agenda.TRAINING, SCALE & EFFICIENCYDevelopment; Foundational

2011ReLU, dropout & practical depthTwo cheap tricks — sparse activations, random deletion — made deep nets trainable without pretraining scaffolds. Simplicity beat cleverness.TRAINING, SCALE & EFFICIENCYDevelopment; Foundational

2014-2017Adam → AdamWAdaptive moments became the default optimizer; AdamW's decoupled weight decay became the durable modern variant. A thousand challengers later, the family remains stubbornly dominant.TRAINING, SCALE & EFFICIENCYDevelopment; Foundational

2015Batch normalizationMini-batch statistics stabilized and accelerated deep-network training, becoming a standard ingredient in convolutional networks and the ResNet lineage.TRAINING, SCALE & EFFICIENCYDevelopment; Foundational

2016Layer normalizationNormalization across a layer's features removed dependence on batch statistics. It became the normalization backbone of recurrent networks and transformers.TRAINING, SCALE & EFFICIENCYDevelopment; Foundational
2015Knowledge distillationBig teacher → small student. Now the pipeline by which frontier capability reaches phones and open models.TRAINING, SCALE & EFFICIENCYDevelopment; Active

2018Transfer learning eraPretraining followed by task adaptation became a dominant workflow across many domains, reducing but not eliminating from-scratch training and helping create the model-hub economy.TRAINING, SCALE & EFFICIENCYDevelopment; Foundational

2015Self-supervised learningLearning supervisory signals from the data itself: contrastive learning, masked prediction, and predictive pretraining. SimCLR, MAE, wav2vec and BERT made it a shared foundation across vision, speech and language.TRAINING, SCALE & EFFICIENCYDevelopment; Foundational

2019The Bitter LessonSutton's essay: general methods riding compute beat human-crafted cleverness, every time so far. The scaling era's ideology — and its critics' target.TRAINING, SCALE & EFFICIENCYDevelopment; Foundational

2020-2022Scaling laws → ChinchillaLoss falls as a power law in compute, data, parameters (Kaplan 2020); Chinchilla corrected the data ratio (2022). Research became engineering.TRAINING, SCALE & EFFICIENCYDevelopment; Foundational

2021LoRA & parameter-efficient tuningLow-rank adapters: customize a giant model on one GPU. Democratized fine-tuning and powered the open-weight explosion.TRAINING, SCALE & EFFICIENCYDevelopment; Foundational
2022Quantization & sparsityINT8→FP4, pruning and structured sparsity shrink models for deployment while trading off memory, throughput and accuracy.TRAINING, SCALE & EFFICIENCYDevelopment; Active

2022FlashAttention & kernel craftIO-aware exact attention. Hardware-sympathetic algorithms beat clever approximations — and killed the linear-attention wave.TRAINING, SCALE & EFFICIENCYDevelopment; Foundational

2023Data curation & synthetic dataMixtures, dedup, quality filters — then models teaching models (phi, distilled reasoning traces). Data quality as the real moat.TRAINING, SCALE & EFFICIENCYDevelopment; Active

2024Test-time compute scalingThink longer instead of training bigger — the o1 insight. A second scaling axis, with search and verification in the loop.TRAINING, SCALE & EFFICIENCYDevelopment; Hot frontier

2025Efficient RL recipes (GRPO, R1)DeepSeek's cheap RL-for-reasoning stack: frontier capability at a fraction of assumed cost. Efficiency itself as geopolitical disruption.TRAINING, SCALE & EFFICIENCYDevelopment; Hot frontier

2025Continual learning pushNested learning, Titans-style memory, weight consolidation: the 2025–26 assault on catastrophic forgetting. Frontier labs now call it solvable.TRAINING, SCALE & EFFICIENCYDevelopment; Hot frontier
2016Differential privacy in MLProvable privacy budgets for training. Deployed in census and keyboards; a steady niche rather than a wave.TRAINING, SCALE & EFFICIENCYDevelopment; Active

2017Federated learningTraining across devices or organizations without centralizing their raw data. It is deployed in privacy-sensitive settings and remains an active research area in optimization, security, and heterogeneous clients.TRAINING, SCALE & EFFICIENCYDevelopment; Active

2019Deep learning theory (NTK, double descent)Why do overparameterized nets generalize? NTK, double descent, lottery tickets — insight-rich, prediction-poor. Theory still trails practice by years.TRAINING, SCALE & EFFICIENCYDevelopment; Active

2026Sleep & memory consolidationResearch direction: develop principled offline consolidation that transfers episodic experience into durable behavior without destructive forgetting. Long context and external memory address related but different problems.TRAINING, SCALE & EFFICIENCYOpen direction; Open direction

1954-1966Georgetown MT demo → ALPACRussian→English demo promised solved-in-5-years; the 1966 ALPAC report axed US funding. NLP's first boom-bust cycle, complete in twelve years.LANGUAGE & LLMsDevelopment; Ended / superseded (legacy)

1957Generative grammarChomsky's formal syntax hierarchies fueled symbolic NLP for decades — and his 'poverty of stimulus' argued pure learning could never acquire language. LLMs reopened the case.LANGUAGE & LLMsDevelopment; Foundational
1966ELIZAWeizenbaum's pattern-matching 'therapist'. The first chatbot — and the first Eliza effect, as users projected understanding onto scripts.LANGUAGE & LLMsDevelopment; Foundational

1972Scripts & conceptual dependencySchank: meaning as canonical structures, stories as scripts. Rich theory with a hand-built ceiling; faded with the statistical turn.LANGUAGE & LLMsDevelopment; Dormant

1975HMM speech recognitionJelinek's statistical turn ('every time I fire a linguist, performance goes up'). Ruled speech for 35 years — then deep nets retired it.LANGUAGE & LLMsDevelopment; Ended / superseded (legacy)

1980n-gram language modelsCount word sequences, predict the next. Powered search and speech for decades — the ancestor LLMs obliterated and descend from.LANGUAGE & LLMsDevelopment; Ended / superseded (legacy)

1975Vector-space information retrievalDocuments and queries represented as weighted term vectors made ranked search practical. This classical retrieval lineage runs through Watson and into retrieval-augmented generation.LANGUAGE & LLMsDevelopment; Foundational
